THESE PETITIONS ARE COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE R. NATARAJ  ORAL ORDER
Criminal Petition No.5771/2025

is filed praying to quash the FIR in Cr.No.109/2025 by respondent No.1/State for the offences punishable under Sections 115(2), 118(1), 189(1), 190, 191(1), 351(2), 352 and 74 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (henceforth referred to as 'BNS, 2023' for short).

2. Criminal Petition No.3895/2025 is filed praying to quash C.C.NO.19/2025 in Cr.No.163/2024 pending on the file of the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Shivamogga for the offences punishable under Sections 189(3), 191(2), 126(2), 115(2), 352, 351(2), 190 of BNS, 2023.
3.

Criminal Petition No.5590/2025 is filed praying to quash the FIR in Crime No.121/2024 registered by respondent NC: 2026:KHC:13733 HC-KAR No.1 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 pending before XXXVII Addl.Judge, Small Causes Court, City Court Complex, Bangalore City.

"The petitioners and respondent No.2 humbly submit as follows:
1.

The Petitioners have filed the above Criminal Petitions seeking to quash the FIR(s)
and to close further proceedings in the connected matters, as detailed below:
a) In Crl.P.No.5771/2025 arising out of Crime No.109/2024, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 115(2), 118(1), 189(1), 190, 191(1), 351(2), 352 and 74 of BNS read on the basis of a complaint lodged by Respondent no.2 before the Azeem Mohammad Haniph Khalipha vs The State Of Karnataka on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105902299/

c) In Crl.P.No.3895/2025 arising out of C.C.No.19/2025, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 189(3), 191(2), 126(2), 115(2), 352(2), 190 of BNS on the basis of a complaint lodged by Respondent No.2 before the Respondent No.1 Police Station.

sentences.text: Upon the intervention of the mediator, the parties have amicably resolved their disputes.

In view of the settlement arrived at between them, Respondent No.2 has no objection to the present petition and the above- mentioned connected matters being allowed, and to the quashing of the FIR(s) as well as the closure of further proceedings against the petitioners in both connected matters herein.

3. It is submitted that Respondent No.2, have received today a Demand Draft bearing number "011640" of Axis Bank dated 27.02.2026 for a sum of Rs.6,31,000/- (Rupees Six Lakh Thirty-One Thousand Only) from Petitioner No.1 towards full and final settlement of all claims in this matter and the connected matters and also exchanged the articles, jewels before the mediation.
NC: 2026:KHC:13733 HC-KAR 4.

The petitioners and the respondent No.2 state that the aforesaid settlement between them is full and final and that neither the respondent No.2 nor the petitioner will have any claims, including monetary claims, against each other.
The petitioners and the respondent No.2 state that this joint compromise application for settlement is filed out of their free will and consent.

5. The Petitioners and Respondent No.2 in Crl.P.No.5590/2025 further submit that they have mutually agreed to dissolve their marriage in O.S.No.80/2025 pending before the Hon'ble Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Channagiri, and in pursuance thereof, they shall execute a Khulanama in accordance with Mohammadan law.

This understanding forms part of the overall settlement, and both parties affirm that the same is entered into with free will and consent, without any force,
coercion, or undue influence.

6. In view of the settlement arrived between the parties, before mediation the parties hereby submit that this petition along with both the connected matters may kindly be allowed and the criminal proceedings be quashed.

WHEREFORE, it is prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to allow this application and quash the FIR(s) and entire proceedings in this petition along with connected matters, to meet the ends of justice."

sentences.text: In view of the fact that the offences alleged against the petitioners in all these petitions are not heinous and are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life, hence, the application filed by the accused for compounding the offences deserves to be considered favourably.
6. The petitioners as well as the complainant/respondent No.2 - Mr. Sharfudeen are present along with his daughter - Mrs.Hifzia Noorain.
They admit the terms of the application and in token of their acceptance of the terms of the application, they have affixed their signatures to the order sheet of this Court.
As stated in the application, the petitioners have handed over a demand draft for a sum of Rs.6,31,000/- to Mrs.Hifzia Noorain and the receipt of the same is acknowledged by her.

7. In view of the above, these petitions are allowed and in terms of application for compounding the offences alleged against the petitioners; (i) in Crime No.109/2024 on the file of Prl.Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC Court, Channagiri, Davangere; (ii) in C.C.No.19/2025 arising out of Crime No.163/2024 on the file of Prl.Civil Judge (Sr.Dn) and CJM - 11 - NC: 2026:KHC:13733 HC-KAR Court, Shimoga District, Shimoga and (iii) in Crime No.121/2024 on the file of 37th Addl. Judge, Small Causes Court, City Court Complex, Bangalore City, are compounded and the petitioners are set free.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Upon the intervention of the mediator, the parties have amicably resolved their disputes.
5. The Petitioners and Respondent No.2 in Crl.P.No.5590/2025 further submit that they have mutually agreed to dissolve their marriage in O.S.No.80/2025 pending before the Hon'ble Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Channagiri, and in pursuance thereof, they shall execute a Khulanama in accordance with Mohammadan law.
This understanding forms part of the overall settlement, and both parties affirm that the same is entered into with free will and consent, without any force,
coercion, or undue influence.
6. In view of the settlement arrived between the parties, before mediation the parties hereby submit that this petition along with both the connected matters may kindly be allowed and the criminal proceedings be quashed.
In view of the fact that the offences alleged against the petitioners in all these petitions are not heinous and are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life, hence, the application filed by the accused for compounding the offences deserves to be considered favourably.
They admit the terms of the application and in token of their acceptance of the terms of the application, they have affixed their signatures to the order sheet of this Court.
As stated in the application, the petitioners have handed over a demand draft for a sum of Rs.6,31,000/- to Mrs.Hifzia Noorain and the receipt of the same is acknowledged by her.
